<!-- Generated by tools/cli-reference.py from `backdown search --help`. Edit the help in crates/backdown-cli (or the notes in the script) and run it again. -->


```text
backdown search [OPTIONS] [Q]...
```

## Arguments

`[Q]...`
: Words to find (all of them; a phrase in quotes).

## Options

`--kind <KIND>`
: Only messages, tables or rows.

`--build`
: Build or update the index first (the service does this after each scan).

`--force`
: With --build: index everything again, not only drives scanned since.

`--depth <DEPTH>`
: How much to index from now on: off, headers (the default) or full.

`--limit <LIMIT>`
: Default: `50`.

`--json`
: Print it as JSON, for scripts.

Also takes the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

Names are found by the search box and `find`; this searches inside things. Mail: every message's subject, sender, recipients and date, from Dovecot's own index (`dovecot.index.cache`) where a mailbox has one, else from the message files (headers only). Dumps and SQLite files: every table with its columns (and which columns the database indexed for full text), and at `--depth full` the text in the rows, text-typed columns only, up to 64 MiB a file. A SQLite full-text table (FTS3/4/5) is searched in place, through SQLite itself. The index keeps no copy of the text, only where each hit is. The service indexes after each recognition; `--build` does it now, skipping what is already indexed for the same scan.

## Examples

```sh
backdown search invoice 2021
# a phrase, and only mail
backdown search "garden work" --kind message
# build the index now, then see what is indexed
backdown search --build
backdown search
# index the text in rows too, from the next build on
backdown search --depth full --build
```
